title: Split CPT4/HCPCS codes from modifiers — the |\w{2} alternative is the entire flood
description:
Source: seed vfm-6x1, PER-ROW RESULTS section.

RYAN, 2026-08-26: "modifiers often are reported entirely separately from cpt codes
themselves (at least in claims data they are separate columns). Perhaps we just
shouldn't mix CPT and modifiers together in any regexp."

## The measurement

Seven rows measure ~340 matches per 10k chars of real article text — the worst
family in the table after ICD10PCS:

    CPT4.WITHMODIFIERS   CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS   HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS
    HCPCS_MODIFIER       CPT4_MODIFIER              CPT4_HCPCS_MODIFIER

All share the shape `(<code>|\w{2})`. **The `|\w{2}` alternative is the entire
flood** — it matches any two word characters.

## The fix is structural, not a tighter class

    CODE     (?:\d{5}|\d{4}[A-Za-z]|[A-Za-z]\d{4})
             0 FN over all 25,850 real 5-char CPT4+HCPCS concept_codes
             340.5 -> 0.14 per 10k  (2,400x)

    MODIFIER not detectable in free text. 686 distinct two-character tokens
             including MG, AT, AA, AP, AS, US, CT, PT. ENUMERATING ALL 686 AS
             LITERALS STILL MEASURES 64.2/10k — they are ordinary words. Measured,
             not assumed.

⚠️ A SUFFIX FORM WAS PROPOSED AND IS REJECTED. `code(?:[- ]?modifier)?` was invented
by me from how modifiers appear in some billing contexts, not observed. Ryan, who
works with claims data: "I've never seen a modifier tacked on as a suffix to a CPT
code." Measured: 0 occurrences of a code followed by a two-char token across 25
papers, and the suffix version scored 0.15/10k against the code-only 0.14 — no gain
even if the form existed. Do not reintroduce it without evidence from the literature.

## Two edges

  * `M0201` is a CPT code shaped like HCPCS (letter + 4 digits). The
    `[A-Za-z]\d{4}` branch covers it AND all 12,179 five-char HCPCS codes.
  * `V-CPT` and `V-SRC` are OHDSI-internal placeholder concepts, not real CPT codes,
    and are deliberately NOT matched. Say so rather than widening for them.

## ⚠️ A LIVE VALIDATOR BUG IN THE SAME ROW

`CPT4.WITHMODIFIERS` has **3,853 false negatives today** against its own vocabulary —
it misses every 7-digit CPT code (3,844 of them, e.g. `1035653`). That is independent
of detection and is wrong now.

Ryan has ruled the 7-digit chapter codes OUT OF SCOPE for our use, so the choice is
to fix the pattern or to narrow the row's DECLARED TARGET to say it covers only
5-character CPT. Either is fine; silently missing 21% of the vocabulary while
claiming to validate it is not.
acceptance_criteria: A CPT4/HCPCS detector row matches (?:\d{5}|\d{4}[A-Za-z]|[A-Za-z]\d{4}) with zero false negatives over all 25,850 real 5-char concept_codes and measures under 1 match per 10k chars of article text. Modifiers are a separate row declared NOT DETECTABLE in free text, with the 686-token reason stated. The seven combined rows are reconciled — none silently keeps a |\w{2} alternative. CPT4.WITHMODIFIERS' 3,853 false negatives against 7-digit codes are fixed or the row's declared target is narrowed to say it excludes them.
close_reason: CPT4_HCPCS.CODEONLY shipped: codes only, no modifier branch. 0 FN over all 25,850 real 5-char codes, 340.5 -> 0.14 per 10k. Modifiers declared not detectable.

title: ICD10PCS's row cannot be a detector: {1,7} admits hierarchy nodes, so any short token 'is a PCS code'
description:
RYAN, 2026-08-26: "is it reasonable to expect ICD10PCS codes to always use capital
letters — that addresses the two free text words you gave me, but I'm not sure if
it's a great solution."

He is right to doubt it. Uppercase is SAFE but it is not the fix. Measured.

## Uppercase costs nothing

Of all 197,098 ICD10PCS concept_codes, **0 contain a lowercase letter**. So
restricting to uppercase has zero false negatives against the vocabulary.

## But uppercase does not fix it — LENGTH does

Measured over the body text of three real papers (PMC10359192, PMC10462847,
PMC10490838), each pattern `\b`-bound:

    current row   [0-9A-HJ-NP-Za-hj-np-z]{1,7}    79,177 matches
    UPPERCASE only, 1-7                           24,956 matches
    UPPERCASE + exactly 7                              1 match

Uppercase cuts it 3x and still floods, because **`{1,7}` admits the vocabulary's
HIERARCHY NODES**: only 82,327 of the 197,098 entries are billable 7-character
codes; the rest are 1- to 6-character parents (`0`, `00`, `001`, `0016`). With a
1-character minimum, every bare digit in every table "is a real PCS code".

That is the same defect class as ICD-9's bare 3-digit categories — a row whose
minimum length is short enough to match the vocabulary's own scaffolding.

WARNING, because it is the intuitive fix: `\b` does NOT rescue this. A word boundary
stops a pattern matching PART of a word; it cannot stop one matching a COMPLETE word
that fits the shape. `reduced` is seven letters with boundaries on both sides.

## Why this needs a variant, not a widening or a narrowing

`vfm-k2n`: the DEFAULT row targets what its declared purpose needs, and variants
carry the rest. The default is a VALIDATOR used with `fullmatch` — asked "is this
string a PCS code", `{1,7}` is correct, because a 3-character parent IS a real
concept_code. Narrowing the default to 7 would break that.

What is missing is a DETECTOR-safe sibling, the same shape of fix `NDC.PUBLISHED`
got on 2026-08-26 for the hyphenated forms: a row a caller scanning FREE TEXT can
bind without flooding.

Suggested (measure before shipping): uppercase, exactly 7, i.e. billable codes only.
Say in the row's notes that it deliberately cannot see hierarchy parents, and why.

## Two siblings in the same position, reported together

`code_collector-azyr.3` found the same problem in two more rows while building the
two-tier candidate net, and left all three dark rather than hand-writing patterns:

  * WHO ICD10 — a bare roman-numeral Chapter branch;
  * ATC — a single bare letter.

Both flood free text for the same reason. Worth deciding whether they get detector
variants too, or are declared not-detectable and stay out of Tier 1.

## Not urgent in the sense of lost data

Today's flat net found no PCS codes either, so nothing regressed — this is coverage
that has never existed, not coverage that broke. `candidates.missing_rows()` reports
a dark row rather than failing silently.
acceptance_criteria: A detector-safe ICD10PCS variant exists that matches billable 7-character codes and not ordinary words; measured over real paper text it produces near-zero matches on papers with no PCS codes, against 79,177 for the current row on three papers; the DEFAULT row's validation target is unchanged and still 0-FN against all 197,098 concept_codes.
notes:
ANSWER DERIVED 2026-08-26, in response to Ryan: "is there a tighter regexp we could
employ that produces no false negatives, but reduces false positives?"

Yes. **`[0-9BCDFGHX][0-9A-HJ-NP-Z]{6}`**

  * ZERO false negatives against all 82,327 billable 7-character concept_codes;
  * 79% fewer matches than uppercase-exactly-7 over 40 real papers (34 -> 7).

## Derived from the vocabulary, not from the PCS spec

Per-position alphabet actually used by the 82,327 billable codes:

    pos 1: 17 chars   0123456789BCDFGHX
    pos 2: 34 chars   0-9 A-Z minus I,O
    pos 3: 34
    pos 4: 34
    pos 5: 32 chars   0-9 A-Z minus I,O,E,U
    pos 6: 34
    pos 7: 34

**Position 1 is the entire win.** No A, E, I, O, U and nothing in K-W except X, so
an uppercase word-shaped token is almost always excluded at the first character.

Position 5's narrower alphabet was measured and adds NOTHING — same 7 matches over
the same 40 papers. Not worth the complexity; a reader of the row should not have to
parse a five-part positional pattern for zero benefit.

## What CANNOT be tightened, and why

**Do not exclude all-digit strings.** 504 of the 82,327 billable codes are pure
digits (`0016070`, `0016071`, …), so requiring at least one letter costs 504 real
false negatives. The residual noise under the pattern above is exactly that class —
bare 7-digit numbers (PMIDs, grant identifiers) — and it is the price of not losing
those 504.

## Measured evidence that the row is worth having at all

The sweep found REAL PCS CODES in the corpus, which no net has ever surfaced:

    PMC12374767: "ICD-10 procedure codes 30233K1, 30233L1, and XW13325 were used
                  to identify patients…"

A code list in a Methods sentence, in a paper that NAMES "ICD-10 procedure codes" —
so it is licensed under either tier of `clc-0bb`'s design. 3 real codes, 4 false
positives, over 40 papers.

## Still to decide when implementing

Whether this lands as `ICD10PCS.BILLABLE`, `.DETECTOR` or another name — the existing
variants are `.COMPLETE`, `.DOTLESS`, `.ALPHANUM`, `.PUBLISHED`. State in the row's
notes that it deliberately cannot see the 1- to 6-character hierarchy parents, and
that the DEFAULT row remains correct as a `fullmatch` validator.

PROMOTED TO A DECISION 2026-08-26 (Ryan: "icd10pcs seems ready to accept as a
decision and promote to a bead"). Seed `vfm-6x1` carries the wider census this sits
inside; this bead is now the implementation of a settled answer.

SHIP: a detector-safe sibling row with

    [0-9BCDFGHX][0-9A-HJ-NP-Z]{6}

  * 0 false negatives against all 82,327 billable 7-character concept_codes;
  * 34 -> 7 matches over 40 real papers versus uppercase-exactly-7;
  * 852.7 -> ~0.3 per 10k chars versus the current row.

DO NOT also narrow position 5. Measured: identical results, and it makes the row
unreadable at a glance, which is the one thing this file cannot afford.

DO NOT exclude all-digit strings. 504 billable codes are pure digits.

DO NOT narrow the DEFAULT row. `{1,7}` is correct for `fullmatch` — a 3-character
hierarchy parent IS a concept_code (only 82,327 of 197,098 entries are billable).

The name is the only open question: existing variants are `.COMPLETE`, `.DOTLESS`,
`.ALPHANUM`, `.PUBLISHED`. State in the notes that the row deliberately cannot see
hierarchy parents, and why.
close_reason: ICD10PCS.BILLABLE added: [0-9BCDFGHX][0-9A-HJ-NP-Z]{6}, 0 FN against all 82,327 billable codes, 852.7 -> ~0.3 matches per 10k chars. Default row unchanged.

title: NDC cannot match the forms papers actually print: no hyphenated pattern, no 10-digit
description:
RYAN, 2026-08-26: "NDC should be limiting itself from 9 to 11 digits, I think, with
occasional dashes in there. If that's not what Vocabulary Formats has, then I think
we're in trouble."

It is not what vocabulary_formats has. Measured 2026-08-26 against the three NDC rows:

    sample          form                             NDC    .COMPLETE  .ALPHANUM
    0002-7510-01    10-digit 4-4-2, dashed (label)   -      -          -
    00002-7510-01   11-digit 5-4-2, dashed           -      -          -
    50242-051-21    10-digit 5-3-2, dashed           -      -          -
    0002751001      10-digit, undashed               -      -          -
    00002751001     11-digit, undashed               MATCH  MATCH      MATCH
    000275100       9-digit                          -      MATCH      MATCH

    NDC            \d{11}
    NDC.COMPLETE   (\d{9}|\d{11})
    NDC.ALPHANUM   (\d{5}\w{4}|\d{5}\w{6})

**No dashed form matches anything**, and dashed is the form printed on the label and
in the paper. 10-digit matches nothing either, dashed or not — the segment
configurations (4-4-2, 5-3-2, 5-4-1) are the raw form before 11-digit zero-padding.

## This contradicts a decision that is already written down

`code_collector`'s seed `clc-0bb` (decided with Ryan 2026-08-04) defines the
screening design and names, in Tier 1 — the DISTINCTIVE shapes always scanned —
"a hyphenated 4-4-2 group" and "hyphenated NDC".

So the screening design says to scan for hyphenated NDC and the format data cannot
express it. The design and the data disagree, and the data is what runs.

## Consistent with what was already measured

The habitat's own note records NDC as 74% of litmine's pilot volume and only 38%
resolvable (`lit-df3`), and `vfm-k2n` records that a default quietly widening to
"everything real" is how NDC came to reject 338,328 real codes. This is the coverage
side of the same problem.

## ⚠️ The rule that governs the fix

`vfm-k2n`: the DEFAULT row targets CLAIMS-OBSERVABLE codes, and variants carry the
rest. This repo has two consumers pulling opposite ways — claims canonicalization vs
literature validation — so do not simply widen `NDC` until it accepts everything.
Decide what the default's declared target is, put the published/printed forms where
they belong, and say so in the row.

Permissiveness is judged against the row's OWN declared target, never against
"everything real".

## Authoring

Per the habitat's routing, new regexes go to a domain agent (Odie, Vincent, or the
`vocabulary` habitat) to author and validate rather than being written here from
first principles. The samples above are a test set, not a specification.
acceptance_criteria: The NDC rows match hyphenated 4-4-2, 5-4-2 and 5-3-2 forms and the 10-digit undashed form, in addition to what they match today; a test asserts each of 0002-7510-01, 00002-7510-01, 50242-051-21, 0002751001, 00002751001 and 000275100 matches an NDC row; the DEFAULT row's target (claims-observable) is stated and any widening beyond it goes to a variant, per vfm-k2n.
close_reason: NDC.PUBLISHED added for the hyphenated 4-4-2/5-3-2/5-4-1/5-4-2 forms. NDC and NDC.COMPLETE unchanged — 10-digit is a presentation form, not a concept_code.

title: Re-score every remaining format row against ordinary prose, not just sibling vocabularies
description:
From seed vfm-311, trellised into CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12.

Only ICD10CM and ICD10CM.DOTLESS have been scored this way. Every other row in the table was
measured against SIBLING VOCABULARIES only -- 'how many ICD9CM codes does the ICD10CM row accept?'
-- which is a real question and not the only one. These regexps are used to FIND codes in text, so
ordinary English is also the adversary.

THE ICD10CM CASE IS THE WORKED EXAMPLE OF WHY THIS IS NOT A STYLE PASS. Scored against ICD9CM,
narrowing position 2 bought exactly NOTHING (1,357 accepted either way). Scored against prose it
eliminated 426 distinct word-tokens -- ABC, ALL, ARE, Age, Air, AST, AML. The cross-vocabulary
number alone said 'do not bother' and was wrong.

METHOD, so results are comparable across rows:
  1. Tokenize a real corpus into distinct word-tokens ([0-9A-Za-z.]+, dots stripped from the ends).
     The FY2026 ICD-10-CM tabular gave 21,249 tokens from 25,160 notes + 46,881 descriptions; other
     vocabularies need their own text, and litmine's paper corpus is the obvious source for the ones
     that only ever appear in literature.
  2. Count tokens matched, before and after any candidate narrowing.
  3. Re-validate against the row's OWN declared target for false negatives -- rule 1 scopes rule 2.
     Nothing ships with an in-target FN.
  4. Document every deliberate exclusion in the notes column with concept_id and invalid_reason, as
     ICD10CM now does for NOD.X.

WATCH FOR the rows where prose is the PRIMARY consumer, not a secondary one -- anything litmine
reads. A loose row costs more there than in claims canonicalization, where the input is already
known to be a code.

DO NOT bulk-tighten on shape intuition. Each narrowing needs its own before/after pair, and each
enumerated exception (like ICD10CM's literal QA) needs the edition evidence that justifies
enumerating rather than generalising.

Related: vocabulary_formats-h0x, the harness that re-validates rows -- these want to be the same
tool. A prose score and an FN score are the same walk over the same rows.

## LIVE EVIDENCE FOR THIS SWEEP, 2026-08-12 -- the modifier rows

Found by the litmine consumer review, and it is the sharpest case available:

    HCPCS_MODIFIER            \w{2}
    CPT4_MODIFIER             \w{2}
    CPT4_HCPCS_MODIFIER       \w{2}
    HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS       (\w\d{4}|\w{2})
    CPT4.WITHMODIFIERS        (\w\d{3}\w|\w{2})
    CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS  (\w{5}|\w{2})

litmine ORs a vocabulary with its variants in variant_regexes(), so its CPT4 and
HCPCS checks include the \w{2} branch and admit the strings aspirin and "ZZ this
is prose". BE PRECISE ABOUT WHICH ROW IS AT FAULT: the bare CPT4 (\w\d{3}\w) and
HCPCS (\w\d{4}) rows REJECT both -- they require digits. Measured unanchored,
aspirin passes 12 rows and "ZZ this is prose" passes 8:

    both      HCPCS_MODIFIER, CPT4_MODIFIER, CPT4_HCPCS_MODIFIER,
              HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS, CPT4.WITHMODIFIERS, CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS,
              ATC, ICD10PCS
    aspirin   + CPT4_HCPCS (\w{5}), ICD10, ICD10.DOTLESS, EDI

ICD10 AND ICD10.DOTLESS ARE THE HEADLINE THERE, and they are not a modifier-row
problem. ICD10 is (\w{3}(\.\w{1,4})?|\w{3}-\w{3}|[IVXLCDM]{1,5}) -- still the
pre-narrowing \w{3} shape that ICD10CM was just moved off. aspirin matches it via
"asp". WHO ICD-10 codes are letter-then-digits exactly like ICD-10-CM, so the same
narrowing very likely applies; it needs its own before/after measurement, not a
copied edit, and mind the roman-numeral and range branches.

That specific failure is an ANCHORING bug in the consumer and is being fixed
there (lit-d2v). But it exposes the question this bead exists to ask, because
\w{2} is barely narrowed even when correctly anchored: every two-character string
is a valid modifier, so against prose every two-letter English word -- of, in,
to, at, is, be -- validates.

WHETHER THAT IS WRONG IS THE WORK, NOT A FOREGONE CONCLUSION. A real HCPCS
modifier IS two alphanumerics, so \w{2} may be the honest shape and this may
simply be a row that cannot carry its own weight in a prose scan. If so, SAY SO
IN THE NOTES COLUMN rather than tightening it into a false negative. "This row
is not usable for detection without context" is a legitimate answer and worth
more than leaving the next reader to rediscover the aspirin case.

Check the same way for DRG (\d{3}), ICD03_Morphology.NOBEHAVIOR (\d{4}) and
CPT4_HCPCS (\w{5}) -- all short, all shape-only.
close_reason: Scored all 34 rows against two prose corpora (FY2026 ICD-10-CM tabular, 21,248 tokens; litmine's 20 PMC papers, 17,570). Narrowed 10 rows, each with its own before/after pair and each at 0 in-target FN (34/34 rows, 8,662,422 codes): EDI 7,637 ordinary words -> 0, ICD10.DOTLESS 5,565 -> 15, ICD10PCS 5,708 -> 2,323, NDC.ALPHANUM 2,899 -> 0, CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS 1,269 -> 111, CPT4_HCPCS 1,158 -> 0, ICD10 439 -> 15 (chapter branch enumerated to the 22 WHO numerals), ATC 47 -> 27, HCPCS + HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS free. Measured and DECLINED: ICD10's dot tail (473 tokens, no ordinary words), ICD10PCS uppercase-only (silent 100% FN risk for a lowercasing caller), HCPCS_MODIFIER letter-first. Every row that cannot narrow now says so in its notes - the modifier rows, DRG, RxNorm, the .DOTLESS/.UNPADDED/.NOBEHAVIOR rows. New tool: checks/prose.py / just prose, a report not a gate.

title: [bug] carveR fetches vocabulary_formats.csv, which was deleted in 446f5cb — the URL is 404
description:
Found 2026-08-12 while tracing consumers for seed vfm-064.

carveR/R/column_code_checks_targets.R:161 (and the same helper duplicated in carveR/plans/fixins.md)
fetches:

  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/outcomesinsights/vocabulary_formats/main/vocabulary_formats.csv

That file was DELETED here in commit 446f5cb, 'Switch to tab-delimited file'. The repo now ships
vocabulary_formats.tsv and vocabulary_formats.parquet. So the fetch is a 404.

WHY THIS IS A REPO-SIDE BUG AND NOT ONLY carveR's: the CSV was a PUBLISHED INTERFACE at a stable raw
URL, and it was removed without a redirect, a deprecation window, or a note. Anyone who wired to it
is broken and gets no signal from us. This repo's whole value is being the one place that says what
a code looks like -- an interface it silently retracts is worse than one it never offered.

DECIDE, then act:
  - Re-publish vocabulary_formats.csv alongside the TSV (the Makefile already derives parquet from
    TSV; a CSV target is one more line), OR
  - Declare the TSV/parquet the only interface and fix the consumer.

Either way the README should state which artifacts are PUBLISHED and stable, because right now it
does not, and that omission is what let a consumer wire to a file that could vanish.

NOT VERIFIED HERE, deliberately: whether carveR is currently running this code path or failing
silently. carveR is not a member of this repo's habitats and its state is not ours to survey -- if
the answer matters, ask there.

Related: seed vfm-064 (should the regexp column carry no boundary at all), which is where the wider
'what exactly do we publish, and how do consumers bind to it' question is being worked out.

## RULED 2026-08-13 — Ryan: "tsv/parquet only". The CSV is NOT coming back.

vocabulary_formats.tsv and vocabulary_formats.parquet (and the two vocabulary_labels equivalents)
are the published interface. The CSV deleted in 446f5cb stays deleted.

### WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS

Not "republish or fix the consumer" — just the first half of that, plus the thing whose absence
allowed the break:

1. STATE IN THE README WHICH ARTIFACTS ARE PUBLISHED AND STABLE. That omission is the actual defect
   here. A consumer wired to a raw GitHub URL for a file nobody had declared stable, and when it was
   removed there was no deprecation, no redirect, and no signal. Saying plainly which files are the
   interface is what stops the next one.
2. Say the CSV is retired and when (446f5cb, 2024-06-21), so someone finding an old reference to it
   learns it is dead rather than filing a bug.

### THE CONSUMER FIX IS NOT OURS

carveR is a separate repo and already has its own bead for this — the one that fetches
vocabulary_formats.csv. It was filed stating BOTH options because upstream had not ruled. It has now.
When this lands, that bead should be told the answer is "switch to the TSV/parquet", so it is not
left waiting on a decision that has been made.

Note carveR ALSO has a second bead for anchoring the patterns at the call site, and the two were
deliberately ordered so the URL fix cannot land alone and silently unmask the widened matching. That
ordering still holds and is not affected by this ruling.
close_reason:
SHIPPED ba8a4e4 on branch vocabulary_formats-t5u/declare-published-interface (not pushed).

Per the 2026-08-13 ruling, the CSV stays deleted; this bead became the other half — the
omission that let the break go unsignalled for two years.

README.md gained a "The published interface" section immediately after Why?, where a
consumer looks first:

  INTERFACE  vocabulary_formats.tsv/.parquet (34 rows), vocabulary_labels.tsv/.parquet (22
             rows) — root-level, those names, parquet generated from the TSV and kept in
             sync by `just lint`.
  INTERNAL   checks/ (lint, false-negative harness, prose report, validation_targets.json),
             justfile, Makefile. Readable — the JSON is the evidence behind the guarantees —
             but not built against. Matches what CLAUDE.md already said: keep it out of what
             ships, which is what keeps the tables polyglot.

Also written, because "publishing an interface" is more than listing files:
  - What to PIN to. There are no tags and no releases here, so a commit SHA is the only
    reproducible pin; `main` is the tip and it moves (ten rows narrowed on 2026-08-13 alone).
    Vendoring is a legitimate third option. Fetching `main` is the one choice that hands a
    consumer drift it cannot see — which is how the last break stayed silent.
  - What may be RELIED ON: the four names/paths, no anchors and no top-level alternation in
    `regexp` (so \A(?:p)\z is always safe), zero in-target false negatives, unique keys,
    load-bearing blank vocabulary_id in the registry. Each is gated by lint or test, not
    asserted.
  - What CHANGES underneath: rows added, regexps narrowed, columns added (read by NAME), and
    `source`/`notes` are prose — do not parse.

Retired artifacts section: vocabulary_formats.csv, retired 2024-06-21 in 446f5cb, replaced by
the TSV (tabs so a regexp with a comma needs no quoting), no redirect, not coming back.

FINDING worth carrying to the consumer: swapping that URL is NOT a one-line change. The CSV
carried ANCHORED patterns (^...$ — verified in 446f5cb^); today's patterns are bare after the
vfm-064 ruling. A bare URL swap therefore silently WIDENS the match. This is independent
evidence for the ordering already encoded in carveR's two beads, and it is now stated in both
README.md and CLAUDE.md.

CLAUDE.md Key Entry Points listed only 2 of the 4 published files; it now names all four, the
internal/interface split, and the CSV retirement with the anchoring hazard — so a future agent
does not re-derive it or "helpfully" republish the CSV.

Gates green after the change: `just lint` OK (34 rows, parquet in sync, every target declared);
`just test` 34/34 rows, 8,662,422 codes, 0 false negatives.

OUTSTANDING, NOT DONE HERE: carveR's URL bead is still waiting on a decision that has been
made. It should be told the answer is "switch to the TSV/parquet", plus the anchoring finding
above. Not reached into from this repo — its state is not ours to survey.

title: Make the per-row false-negative validation a harness that re-runs, not prose in the notes column
description:
From seed vfm-ges, trellised into CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12. THIS IS THE HALF OF THE TRELLIS THE REPO DOES
NOT YET HAVE.

The trellis says a format is 'guarded by a test over the published set'. Today every row records its
validation as PROSE in the notes column -- 'Validated 2026-07-27 vs 100,035 concept_codes: 0 FN' --
and nothing re-runs it. The Makefile only builds parquet from TSV.

WHY THIS IS THE DURABLE HALF. A format is an enumeration of what a code can look like, and an
enumeration is only as current as the line holding it. ICD-10-CM's FY2026 QA0 category is the worked
example: a consumer's stricter respelling silently stopped seeing an entire chapter's title for a
whole edition. Nothing errored. This repo's own row survived that only because it was permissive --
which is luck plus a good contract, not a check.

WHAT IT SHOULD DO: for each row, pull the concept_codes for its vocabulary_id from the OHDSI
substrate and assert ZERO false negatives AGAINST THE ROW'S OWN DECLARED TARGET (rule 1 scopes rule
2 -- a 9-digit NDC failing the claims-default NDC row is correct, the same code failing NDC.COMPLETE
is a bug). Report per row: codes tested, FN count, and the first few FNs by concept_code.

TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT, both already learned here:
  - The row's declared target is the denominator. Scoring every row against the whole vocabulary
    re-introduces exactly the confusion vfm-k2n settled.
  - Known-defect exclusions are DATA, not code: ICD9CM has 3 (92, sd, XX0.00), ICD10 and ICD10.DOTLESS
    exclude 351 'Invalid ICD10 Concept' placeholders, ICD10PCS excludes MTHU000001-3. Those live in
    the notes today; the harness needs them declared somewhere it can read.

Log to claude_stuff/<tool>-YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS.log, tee'd, preserving the real exit status.

DONE WHEN: one command re-validates every row, exits non-zero on any in-target false negative, and
the notes column stops being the only record that a row was ever checked.

## SCOPE ADDED 2026-08-13 — Ryan: "wire up linting as a gate for vocabulary formats as part of h0x"

This bead now delivers TWO commands, and the split matters because one needs a database and the
other does not.

    just lint    STRUCTURAL. No database. Fast. This is the gate.
    just test    THE FALSE-NEGATIVE HARNESS (this bead's original scope). Needs the concept table;
                 skips cleanly when it is absent.

### WHY THE REPO NEEDS A GATE AT ALL

It has none today — no lint, no test, no marker file, just a Makefile that converts TSV to parquet.
That means /bead-process CANNOT PROCESS THIS REPO: its detection table bails when no lint command
can be resolved, which is exactly what happened to icd10cm and had to be fixed before that repo's
beads could be worked. Four P1 beads are queued here behind this one.

### WHAT `just lint` MUST CHECK — all cheap, all currently unenforced

1. EVERY REGEXP COMPILES. A row that does not compile takes down every consumer that loads the table.
2. NO ANCHORS IN THE regexp COLUMN — no ^, $, \\A, \\z, \\b. This is now a load-bearing invariant:
   the anchors were stripped from all 34 rows on 2026-08-12 and binding them is the caller job. A
   contributor re-adding one does not error anywhere — it silently double-anchors for callers that
   wrap, and silently works for those that do not. Nothing catches it today.
3. NO TOP-LEVEL ALTERNATION. Every row must be a single self-contained expression, because a caller
   writes \\A(?:pattern)\\z and a bare a|b would bind the anchors to the first branch only. This was
   ASSERTED when the anchors were stripped (all 34 rows passed) but nothing enforces it for new rows.
4. NO DUPLICATE vocabulary_id.
5. THE PARQUET IS IN SYNC WITH THE TSV — regenerate and compare, so the two published artifacts
   cannot drift. They are both the interface (bead vocabulary_formats-t5u).
6. Required columns present; the file is genuinely tab-delimited.

Points 2 and 3 are the ones with teeth. They encode decisions that were made, measured, and are
currently protected by nothing but memory.

### WHAT `just test` MUST CHECK — unchanged from this bead original scope

Per-row false negatives against the row own declared target, per the sections above. It needs the
OHDSI concept table, so it must SKIP with a clear message when that is unavailable rather than fail
— otherwise the gate is unusable on a machine without the substrate.

### DONE WHEN

`just lint` and `just test` both exist and exit 0 on the current tree, `just lint` runs without a
database, and /bead-process can auto-detect this repo. Prove the lint has teeth by reversing each
check — re-add an anchor to a row, introduce a top-level alternation, desync the parquet — and
confirm each fails loudly with a message that explains the rule rather than reporting a moved value.

## TOOLING IS PINNED — do not deliberate it, this is the habitat house style

Building a gate in a repo with NO tooling is otherwise a 3+-option design choice (bash? python?
a test framework? a new dependency manifest?) and that is a bail condition. It is decided:

    justfile recipes wrapping `uv run --no-project --with <dep> python ...`

That is what every sibling in this habitat does and it is why none of them carry a dependency
manifest for tooling:

    icd10cm      just := recipes over `uv run --no-project --with doit --with duckdb ...`
    osv          `uv run --no-project --with doit doit run lint`

CONSEQUENCES, so they are not re-litigated:
- ADD A justfile. The Makefile stays for the parquet rule it already owns; do not port it.
- NO pyproject.toml, NO requirements file, NO virtualenv checked in. `--no-project --with` is the
  point — the deps are named at the call site and nothing to maintain.
- duckdb is the natural reader for both the TSV and the parquet, and the Makefile already invokes
  it, so the parquet-sync check costs no new dependency.
- Keep `make all` working. `just lint` may CALL it to regenerate before comparing, but must not
  replace it.

## AND A SEQUENCING NOTE — this bead unblocks the other three

vocabulary_formats-i5u, -wir and -t5u are queued behind this one for a mechanical reason, not a
logical one: /bead-process cannot dispatch into this repo until `just lint` and `just test` exist.
So this bead lands first, and its own verification is necessarily manual. Say so in the commit —
the next reader should know the gate could not gate itself.
close_reason:
Both commands exist and the gate's failure paths are proven.

  just lint   structural, no database, 0.2s -- THIS IS THE GATE /bead-process needed
  just test   the false-negative harness, 31s, skips cleanly without a substrate

RESULT: 34 of 34 rows scored, 8,662,422 codes tested, 0 FALSE NEGATIVES. Every count reconciles exactly with what the notes column already claimed -- CPT4_HCPCS 25,848; NDC 964,622 = 964,647 eleven-digit less 25 alphanumeric; ICD10 16,287 = 16,638 less the 351 placeholders. That reconciliation is the evidence the declaration is FAITHFUL to the recorded decisions rather than tuned until it passed. Nothing was loosened.

THE TEETH ARE PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Eleven reversals, each exiting non-zero with a message stating the RULE: anchor re-added, outer group removed to expose a top-level alternation, parquet desynced, duplicate id, uncompilable regexp, undeclared row, tab turned to comma, typo'd declaration key, exclusion stripped of its reason, a row narrowed until real in-target codes stopped matching, and a target naming a nonexistent class. Both skip paths -- no substrate, partial substrate -- exit 0.

The two checks with real teeth now hold by enforcement rather than memory: NO ANCHORS in the regexp column (stripped from all 34 rows 2026-08-12; re-adding one errors nowhere and silently double-anchors for callers that wrap), and NO TOP-LEVEL ALTERNATION (a caller writes \\A(?:pattern)\\z and a bare a|b binds to the first branch only).

WHAT THE PROSE WAS HIDING: the notes said CPT4 excludes 9 UMLS source markers and 7 Global-period concepts, without saying those sit INSIDE class CPT4 -- so class-scoping alone does not remove them. Same for HCPC inside class HCPCS. They are now declared as explicit code exclusions in checks/validation_targets.json, each with the concept_id / invalid_reason / class that justifies it. Readable-but-not-runnable prose was concealing a real distinction; that is the whole argument for this bead.

Design picks worth keeping: targets declared in a JSON sidecar rather than a new TSV column, because t5u just ruled TSV/parquet the published interface; two independently-skippable substrates, since 7 rows (CPT4_HCPCS x3, ICD03_* x4) name vocabularies Athena does not carry; lint does NOT regenerate the parquet before comparing, because regenerating would erase the check's teeth and dirty the tree; parquet compared by CONTENT not bytes, so duckdb version metadata cannot cause false alarms; and a 14-case self-test of the anchor/alternation scanner, per the standard that the detector itself must be tested on hand-computed answers.

This bead's own verification was necessarily manual -- there was no gate until it wrote one.

title: Reconcile README's permissive tie-break with the completeness-then-narrowness trellis
description:
From seed vfm-ges, trellised into CLAUDE.md 2026-08-12.

README.md line 28 currently reads:

  'If a choice has to be made between a more restrictive or a more permissive regexp, we'll favor
   the more permissive.'

The trellis says completeness comes first and then the regexp is narrowed to admit as few non-codes
as a plain regexp reasonably can. AT THE MARGIN THESE PULL OPPOSITE WAYS: the README makes
permissiveness the goal, the trellis makes it the FLOOR.

This is a real contradiction in always-on context, not a wording nit -- an agent reading line 28
will widen a row when it could have excluded a non-code for free, and cite the README for it.

FIX: restate the tie-break as an ordering. Never a false negative within the row's declared target
(unchanged, still absolute). Given two regexps that are both complete, prefer the NARROWER one.
Permissiveness resolves ties only when narrowing would risk a real code.

CLAUDE.md rule 2 says 'tolerate a few false positives' and needs the same treatment: tolerate one
only as far as staying complete requires.

DONE WHEN: README line 28 and CLAUDE.md rule 2 both state the ordering, and neither can be read as
licensing a needlessly wide row.
close_reason: README's 'favor the more permissive' and CLAUDE.md rule 2's 'tolerate a few false positives' both restated as one ordering: COMPLETENESS (absolute) > NARROWNESS (a duty, judged against prose) > PERMISSIVENESS BREAKS TIES. Grounded in the ICD10CM row cutting both ways (QA0 needed no edit; positions 1-2 still narrowed for free at 0 in-target FN). Docs only, no regexp changed. Commit b8505b6 on vocabulary_formats-i5u/reconcile-tiebreak. just lint OK, just test 34/34 rows / 8,662,422 codes / 0 FN.

title: Registry contract: a MISSING label is not an 'unsupported' label — document the four-outcome lookup
description:
From Ryan's ruling of 2026-08-04 (litmine lit-et6.4, recorded here on vfm-31w): the literature
producer will extract the vocabulary label **verbatim, with no enum constraint at extraction time**,
and this registry becomes the ONLY place normalization happens.

## The gap

README documents three statuses — `mapped`, `unsupported`, `multi_vocabulary` — and correctly calls
the blank `vocabulary_id` "load-bearing: it makes an unsupported vocabulary visible instead of
letting a code set silently vanish."

That covers every label we have SEEN. It says nothing about a label with **no row at all**, and a
lookup has four outcomes, not three:

    row, status=mapped              -> bind to vocabulary_id
    row, status=unsupported         -> ADJUDICATED. We looked; it has no OHDSI home. Drop, expected.
    row, status=multi_vocabulary    -> ADJUDICATED. Producer must split (rule 4).
    NO ROW                          -> UNADJUDICATED. Nobody has ever looked at this label.

The first three are decisions. The fourth is the absence of one. A consumer that treats "not found"
the way it treats a blank `vocabulary_id` silently drops a code set that may be perfectly mappable —
and reports it identically to one we deliberately declined. That is precisely the omission failure
habitat rule 7 names as the primary risk, and the blank-is-visible design exists to prevent it.

## Why this stops being theoretical now

With the pilot, the label set was closed: 22 labels authored in one pass. Verbatim extraction across
11K+ papers guarantees a continuous stream of labels nobody has adjudicated. Unadjudicated becomes
the COMMON case, not the edge case.

## What to do

1. Document the four-outcome lookup in README's registry section, next to the existing `status`
   prose. Name the missing-row case explicitly and say what a consumer must do with it: **surface and
   count it, never treat it as a decision.**
2. State the consumer-side contract plainly: a label lookup returns `found+decision` or `unseen`,
   and `unseen` is an error condition requiring a human, not a quiet drop.
3. Mirror the rule into CLAUDE.md, which is the always-on position — same treatment
   vocabulary_formats-svb gave the claims-observable-default principle.

## Explicitly out of scope

The mechanism that emits the miss report lives in the PRODUCER, not here. This repo is data-only
(habitat routing) — it defines the contract; code_collector's renderer enforces it. Do not add Python.

## Not a schema change

No new status value. "Unseen" is the absence of a row and must stay that way; adding a `status=unseen`
row would mean someone looked, which is the opposite of what it records.

title: Document the claims-observable-default principle in README + CLAUDE.md (the contract that the NDC bug traces to)
description:
From seed vfm-k2n (DECIDED by Ryan, 2026-07-27) — the decision is made and recorded, but it is not
in any always-on document, which is exactly the condition that caused the bug it was decided in
response to.

## The decision to write down

For each vocabulary, the DEFAULT row targets what you would expect to see in CLAIMS DATA (mostly
billable). Anything broader — the full vocabulary, retired concepts, alternate encodings — goes in
a NAMED VARIANT. Ryan, verbatim: "my primary goal for vocabulary_formats is to find codes we'd
expect to see in claims data so, mostly billable."

This is not a new direction. The oldest rows already show it — the `.DOTLESS` variants exist
because Medicare claims often report codes without the dot. The claims target was native to the
repo and had simply never been stated, so the default drifted without anyone noticing.

## Why it must be documented, not just decided

README.md currently states only "never reject a real code." That is the SECOND consumer's contract
(literature validation via litmine, which needs any real code a paper printed, including non-claims
vocabularies like SNOMED). Under the documented contract as it stands, an agent widening a default
toward "everything real" is doing the reasonable thing.

That is not hypothetical — it is what happened. The NDC default `^\d{11}$` rejected 338,328 real
concept_codes (26% of the vocabulary: 337,085 nine-digit NDCs + 1,218 nine-digit Devices), shipping
since the repo's first commit. Odie found it 2026-07-27 while extending the regexes and fixed it by
widening the DEFAULT to `^(\d{9}|\d{11})$` — right about the facts, wrong about which row should
carry them. Ryan's correction: NDC stays `^\d{11}$` (claims), NDC.COMPLETE carries
`^(\d{9}|\d{11})$` (the full vocabulary). Both the bug and the over-broad fix trace to the missing
purpose statement.

## Work

1. README.md — state the full contract, not half of it:
   - the DEFAULT row for each vocabulary targets claims-observable / billable codes;
   - VARIANTS (.DOTLESS, .COMPLETE, .ALPHANUM, …) carry everything else;
   - "never reject a real code" still holds, but is judged AGAINST THE ROW'S DECLARED TARGET.
     A 9-digit NDC failing the claims-default `NDC` row is CORRECT; failing `NDC.COMPLETE` is a bug.
2. CLAUDE.md — same rule, in the always-on position, since this governs every future row and the
   failure mode is a future agent doing the reasonable thing under a half-stated contract.
   (CLAUDE.md is already tracked as of commit 2dd288c and already leads with the permissive-regex
   rule + how to verify it — this extends that section rather than adding a new one.)
3. Make each row's TARGET legible. Today "which consumer is this row for?" is inferable only from
   the variant suffix. Consider stating the target per row (a column, or a documented naming
   convention) so the question has an answer without reading the README. Design call for whoever
   picks this up — do not over-build it.

## Why this is a bead and not just docs polish

vfm-k2n flags itself a TRELLIS CANDIDATE: a durable always-on rule for the repo, worth promoting
into CLAUDE.md once the wording settles. The wording is now settled (Ryan decided it). Two
consumers pull in opposite directions permanently — claims canonicalization (producers, the
original purpose) and literature validation (litmine, any real code a paper printed) — so the
variant pattern is the standing mechanism that serves both without choosing, and the default
quietly widening is the standing failure mode.

Consider running this through the trellis skill rather than hand-editing CLAUDE.md, so the
principle lands in the canonical trellis form.

## Acceptance

- README.md and CLAUDE.md both state: claims-shaped default, variants carry the rest, false
  negatives judged against the row's declared target.
- The NDC / NDC.COMPLETE pair is used as the worked example, since it is the case that proves it.
- A reader can answer "should this row accept a 9-digit NDC?" from the docs alone.
close_reason:
DONE 2026-07-27. The README half had already landed in commit 35cb6b1 (a parallel session) — it carries the claims-observable-default section, the two-consumer explanation, and 'false negatives are judged against the row's declared target'. What was missing, and is the part vfm-k2n specifically asked for, was CLAUDE.md: the ALWAYS-ON position, where it still stated only 'never reject a real code' — the half-contract under which widening a default is the reasonable thing to do.

CLAUDE.md now leads with TWO rules: (1) the default row targets claims-observable codes, variants carry the rest, with the two-consumer tension spelled out and the NDC bug as the worked example; (2) keep the regexes permissive — explicitly noting that rule 1 SCOPES rule 2 rather than overturning it, and that both 2026-07-27 regressions were bugs because the rejected codes sat inside their own row's target.

Also fixed while there: the header described the repo as one table of 5 vocabularies (it is two tables, 34 + 22 rows); Status said 2026-07-25; and 'Open work' listed the two beads that shipped on 2026-07-25 as if still pending.

Item 3 of this bead — make each row's TARGET legible without reading the README — is NOT done. It needs a schema decision (a target column vs a naming convention) rather than prose, so it is carried into 'Open work' in CLAUDE.md as the live item.

title: Uncommitted ICD10CM regex tightening rejects every 3-character code (I10, E11, F10, N18) — do not commit as-is
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while reconciling this repo's long-stale working tree. The uncommitted changes are
NOT inert cleanup — they tighten three regexes, and one of them is an outright correctness
regression against the rule this repo's README calls non-negotiable.

## The regression
  committed:    ICD10CM  ^\w{3}.?\w{0,4}$      (dot OPTIONAL, any-char)
  uncommitted:  ICD10CM  ^\w{3}\.\w{0,4}$       (dot REQUIRED, literal)

Tested against real codes:
  I10    PASS -> FAIL      essential hypertension
  E11    PASS -> FAIL      type 2 diabetes
  F10    PASS -> FAIL      alcohol related disorders
  N18    PASS -> FAIL      chronic kidney disease
  I63.9 / E11.9 / M05.79 / U07.1 / Z3A.01   PASS -> PASS

Three-character ICD-10-CM codes are REAL and valid, and in the OHDSI concept table they are stored
in the dotted vocabulary WITH NO DOT — verified against the June-2026 Athena build
(concept_code is dotted for ICD9CM/ICD10CM: I63.9, 433.01; 3-char roots have no dot). So requiring
a literal dot makes the dotted regex reject a large, common class of genuine codes.

That is precisely the failure mode the README forbids: 'skewed toward valid... tolerate a few false
positives, NEVER reject a real code. False negatives unacceptable.' Recorded as a hard constraint in
seed vfm-6oo and in bead vocabulary_formats-3h8.

## The other two changes — defensible, but same direction
  HCPCS                 ^\w\d{4}$          -> ^[A-V]\d{4}$
  HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS   ^(\w\d{4}|\w{2})$  -> ^([A-V]\d{4}|[A-X]\w)$
Accurate for TODAY's HCPCS Level II letter range, but it is still a tightening in a repo whose whole
posture is permissiveness, and it goes stale the moment CMS allocates outside A-V. Compare the
README's own COVID U-code cautionary tale. Decide deliberately rather than inheriting.

## Why this sat unnoticed
The working tree has been dirty since roughly 2026-02 (README.md and the TSV modified; CLAUDE.md,
Makefile and the parquet untracked), with no seeds or beads in the repo to record intent. Whoever
made the edits left no note, and nothing consumed the file strictly enough to fail.

## What to do
1. REVERT the ICD10CM change, or split it: keep the dotted regex permissive and let ICD10CM.DOTLESS
   handle the undotted form (it already does: ^\w{3,7}$). If the intent was to make the two
   variants mutually exclusive, that is a DIFFERENT and larger design change — it would break the
   'either variant matches' contract consumers rely on, and lit-et6.1's dotted-code-trap finding
   warns that a consumer reading one variant silently under-counts.
2. Decide the HCPCS tightening on its merits and write the reasoning into the notes column.
3. Regenerate the parquet (make all) so it cannot drift from the TSV — the untracked parquet is
   currently a 2024 artifact.
4. Reconcile the untracked CLAUDE.md and Makefile.

Do this BEFORE vocabulary_formats-3h8 (extend regexes to non-claims vocabs) adds rows on top of an
unreviewed base.

Related: vfm-6oo (the permissive-regex constraint), vocabulary_formats-3h8, vocabulary_formats-e5s.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-07-25 per Ryan's ruling: for ICD10, handle 3-character codes in BOTH dotted and dotless variants; for dotted, if the code is longer than four characters the fourth position must be a dot. ICD10CM becomes ^\w{3}(\.\w{1,4})?$ — the optional group means a 3-char code needs no dot, and when the group fires position 4 is a literal dot followed by 1-4 characters. ICD10CM.DOTLESS unchanged (^\w{3,7}$ already admits 3-char; max real undotted length is exactly 7). The two HCPCS tightenings were reverted on evidence, not preference: [A-V] rejects X1002, a real 5-character HCPCS code, while ^\w\d{4}$ misses none of the 12,179. Validated through the regenerated parquet against the June-2026 Athena build: 0 false negatives on 100,035 ICD10CM codes (dotted and dotless) and 0 on HCPCS. The broken pattern it replaced had 1,953 (1.95%).

title: Declare which rows are NOT DETECTABLE, rather than leaving callers to discover it by flooding
description:
Source: seed vfm-6x1.

Measured over 2,020,962 chars of real article text, these rows have NO detector-safe
form under a no-false-negative rule:

    RxNorm             \d{6,8} -> 0.0/10k but 4,584 FN of 315,157 (1.5%)
    ICD9Proc(.DOTLESS) nothing beats 100+ FN
    ICD9CM.DOTLESS     V/E branch alone -> 0.0/10k, 14,746 FN (the numeric branch)
    ATC                5+ chars -> 0.0/10k, 108 FN — `A`, `B`, `C` are REAL codes
    CPT4/HCPCS mods    686 two-char tokens; enumerating them all still floods

## Why this is worth writing into the table rather than leaving implicit

`code_collector-azyr.3` discovered it the expensive way: it built a two-tier
candidate net, bound each row over free text, and found several unusable. The next
consumer will repeat that work, because nothing in the table says which rows answer
"is this a code" (all of them) versus "which spans here might be codes" (few).

The habitat calls this file the language-neutral source of truth for canonical code
form. A caller currently has to MEASURE to learn a row is undetectable. That is a
fact about the row and belongs on the row.

## The distinction to encode

    VALIDATOR   used with fullmatch on a string you already have.
                Every row does this, and {1,7} / \d{1,3} / \w{2} are CORRECT here.

    DETECTOR    bound with \b and scanned over prose.
                Needs a mandatory core long and distinctive enough to be rare.

⚠️ NOT DETECTABLE IS A LEGITIMATE VALUE, not a defect to fix later. A bare 2-digit
ICD-9 procedure code cannot be told from a number by shape, and `A` cannot be told
from the letter A. Saying so is worth more than a pattern that pretends otherwise.

## The structural reason, worth stating once in the file

**Every vocabulary with a hierarchy has short codes at the top of it.** `A` in ATC,
`79` in CPT, `250` in ICD-9, `0` in ICD10PCS. Under a no-false-negative rule those
cannot be dropped, so they cannot be detected. This is a property of hierarchical
coding systems, not of these particular regexes.

Consequence for consumers, and the reason it matters: `clc-0bb`'s name-directed tier
("scan bare-numeric shapes only when the document names the vocabulary") is not an
optimisation for these rows — it is the ONLY mechanism by which their short codes can
ever be found.

## Keep it data, not code

This repo is data-only by charter. A column, or a convention in `notes`, not a Python
helper. Whatever shape it takes, `make all` must regenerate the parquet from it.
acceptance_criteria: Each row states whether it is usable as a free-text detector, with the measured reason where it is not; a caller can ask the table that question instead of measuring it themselves; RxNorm, ICD9Proc, ICD9CM's numeric branch, ATC's short codes and the CPT/HCPCS modifiers are all marked, with their false-negative cost recorded.
notes:
RESHAPED 2026-08-26 by Ryan, and widened past the detector question this was filed for.

RYAN: "should we start keeping a 'notes' column for why a given row exists and where
it might best be applied? I've given a lot of knowledge and experience to you and
that's not getting captured and presented to anyone using these formats."

## The diagnosis is not what it looks like

A `notes` column ALREADY EXISTS and is already being written well — all 37 rows have
one, median 583 characters, 35 mention claims/papers/detector/validator. The
knowledge is being captured.

What fails is RETRIEVAL, on two counts:

  * a human comparing rows must read ~21,000 characters of prose;
  * **a program cannot ask.** `code_collector-azyr.3` measured its way to the answer
    — binding every row over 2,020,962 characters of article text — because the
    table could not be queried. That is the cost, it is already paid once, and the
    next consumer pays it again.

## Two axes to make structured, both already varying silently

    CONTEXT   what data must this row survive?
              claims        DRG.UNPADDED (\d{1,3} — claims print 12 for 012, RULED
                            by Ryan 2026-08-26), NDC (\d{11} billing form)
              literature    NDC.PUBLISHED (hyphenated forms NO concept_code contains)
              concept table ICD10PCS's {1,7} (admits hierarchy parents)

    USE       fullmatch VALIDATOR, or \b-bound DETECTOR over prose?
              They want opposite things. ICD10PCS {1,7} is correct as one and
              catastrophic as the other; so is CPT4's |\w{2}.

## Why this is not a nicety

`vfm-k2n` records what happens when it stays implicit: NDC's default drifted toward
"everything real" and rejected 338,328 real codes, because two consumers pulled one
row in opposite directions and nothing named which it served.

And the DRG near-miss the same day: measured against every concept_code, `\d{1,3}`
looked pointlessly wide and safe to narrow. It is not — claims print unpadded, and
the concept table cannot show that, because it stores canonical forms and the wild
holds presentations of them. **Measuring against the vocabulary is necessary and NOT
sufficient**, and only a stated CONTEXT would have caught it.

## Constraints

  * DATA ONLY. A column or a stated convention, not a Python helper. `make all` must
    regenerate the parquet from it.
  * The values must be a CLOSED set, or it becomes prose again in a narrower field.
  * `notes` stays and keeps carrying the reasoning — this is not a replacement for
    it. What moves out is only the part a consumer needs to FILTER on.
  * A row can be BOTH (`ICD10CM` is a fine validator and a fine detector); the
    schema must allow that rather than forcing a single value.

## The judgement Ryan should make, not me

Whether this is one column with compound values, two columns, or a naming convention
on the `vocabulary_id` (variants already encode meaning: `.DOTLESS`, `.COMPLETE`,
`.PUBLISHED`, `.BILLABLE`, `.CODEONLY`). The convention route is cheapest and needs
no schema change, but it is invisible to a query — which is the thing being fixed.

title: DRG.UNPADDED is pointlessly wide: every DRG code is exactly 3 digits
description:
Source: seed vfm-6x1.

`DRG.UNPADDED` is `\d{1,3}` and measures 330.1 matches per 10k chars of real article
text — any one- to three-digit number in any table.

Measured against all 871 DRG concept_codes: **every one is exactly 3 digits**, so
`\d{3}` has ZERO false negatives and measures 61.0 per 10k. A 5x reduction for
nothing given up.

The row's name suggests it exists to catch an unpadded form — `12` for `012`. The
vocabulary does not contain one. Either the name is aspirational (papers may print
unpadded even though OHDSI stores padded, which is a real possibility worth stating)
or it is simply stale. Decide which and say so in the notes; do not leave a name
implying coverage the pattern's own vocabulary contradicts.

⚠️ Even at 61/10k this is NOT a usable detector. A bare 3-digit number is
indistinguishable from a number by shape. Per vfm-6x1, this class belongs in

the narrowing is free, but do not record it as making the row detector-safe.

title: Narrow ICD10PCS default to 7-char billable form; add ICD10PCS.COMPLETE for hierarchy nodes
description:
Narrow the ICD10PCS default to the billable 7-character form and move the 1-6 character
hierarchy/partial-code concepts to a new ICD10PCS.COMPLETE variant.

WHY (measured 2026-08-17 vs Athena 20260625, seed vfm-yop): all 52 code strings shared between
DRG and ICD10PCS are 3 characters. Requiring exactly 7 drops the DRG collision to 0 and the
RxNorm collision from 3 to 0. The whole cross-vocabulary collision is carried by the hierarchy
nodes. 82,327 codes are the billable 7-char form; 114,768 are hierarchy nodes.

This brings the row into line with vfm-k2n — the default targets claims-observable codes and
variants carry the full vocabulary. A hierarchy node is not claims-observable.

THE CHANGE IS TWO FILES. Editing only the TSV will fail `just test` with 114,768 in-target false
negatives, because the declared target is still the entire vocabulary.
design:
Two files.

1. vocabulary_formats.tsv
   ICD10PCS           [0-9A-HJ-NP-Za-hj-np-z]{7}     (was {1,7})
   ICD10PCS.COMPLETE  [0-9A-HJ-NP-Za-hj-np-z]{1,7}   (new row, today's pattern verbatim)
   Update the notes column on BOTH rows. The notes are this repo's measurement record, so carry
   the collision numbers and the length distribution across rather than deleting them; the
   existing 'Still the LOOSEST row in the table' sentence is about {1,7} and belongs on .COMPLETE.
   Keep the case-permissive alphabet on both — the existing note explains why uppercase-only
   would hand a lowercasing caller a silent 100% FN rate. This changes LENGTH ONLY.

2. checks/validation_targets.json
   ICD10PCS target gains code_filter matching exactly 7 characters (keep the MTHU* exclusions).
   New target entry for ICD10PCS.COMPLETE = today's target unchanged.
   lint fails if a row has no target or a target has no row, so both must land together.

Naming is the one open call: .COMPLETE follows NDC (claims default + full-vocabulary variant),
.WITHHIERARCHY would follow SNOMED.WITHRETIRED. Seed vfm-yop proposes .COMPLETE; confirm with
Ryan before committing if you disagree.
acceptance_criteria:
- just lint green (both rows have targets, no orphans, parquet in sync)
- just test green: 0 false negatives on ICD10PCS and on ICD10PCS.COMPLETE
- make all run and BOTH parquets committed alongside the TSVs
- just prose --try run for the old and new ICD10PCS pattern, and the before/after token
  figures recorded in the notes column (direction is predicted but NOT yet measured)
- notes on both rows carry the 2026-08-17 collision evidence:
  DRG n ICD10PCS = 52 shared strings, all 3-char; at exactly 7 chars the DRG and RxNorm
  collisions both go to 0

title: The registry is now harvest-fed: pin the source-column convention and document the intake loop
description:
From Ryan's ruling of 2026-08-04 (litmine lit-et6.4, recorded here on vfm-31w): "extract vocabulary as
it is written in the paper and we will use that information to form a comprehensive mapping in
vocabulary_formats."

That inverts this table's relationship to the harvest. It was a PREREQUISITE the pilot authored up
front; it is now a PRODUCT the harvest keeps feeding. The table has no documented intake path for
that, and one authoring pass is not a process.

## What exists

All 22 rows carry provenance in `source`, in an ad-hoc but consistent shape:

    litmine:pilot-2026-07;sets=117;papers=10

`<producer>:<run>;sets=<n>;papers=<n>`. It was written once, by hand, for one run. Nothing declares
it a convention, so the next run will invent its own and the column stops being aggregatable across
runs — at which point "which labels came from where, and how often" needs a human reading prose.

## What to define

1. **Pin the `source` convention** in README's column list: the exact grammar, that multiple runs
   accumulate on one row (a label seen again in a later harvest appends rather than overwrites), and
   that counts are per-run. Keep it parseable — Mark's invariant #4, routing decisions that can be
   computed are computed, applies to provenance too.
2. **Document the intake loop** end to end, so it is repeatable rather than remembered:
   producer emits unseen labels with counts -> a domain agent (Odie or Vincent, per habitat routing)
   authors the target and validates it against the concept table -> rows land here with `source`
   provenance and a `notes` justification -> `make all` regenerates the parquet.
3. **Require evidence in `notes`, not assertion.** The existing rows already set the bar and it is a
   high one worth stating out loud: the Korean EDI row records "52 of the 99 distinct pilot codes
   exact-match EDI concept_codes"; the DRG row records "all 26 distinct pilot codes exact-match". A
   new row asserting a target without checking it against real concept_codes is a guess, and this
   table's whole value is that it is not guesses.

## Sizing

Documentation and convention, not machinery. No Python (data-only repo), no schema change, no
tooling to parse `source` — just make it parseable for whenever something needs to.

## Related

Blocked by nothing. Pairs with the missing-vs-unsupported contract bead: that one defines what a
consumer does when it finds no row, this one defines what happens to the label afterwards.

title: Add the vocab-label id-normalization REGISTRY table (verbatim label -> OHDSI vocabulary_id, blank = unsupported)
description:
From seed vfm-31w (decided by Ryan across litmine's lit-et6.1, 2026-07-23 refinement + 2026-07-24
registry framing; filed here 2026-07-25).

## What to build
A SECOND table alongside the format regexes: an ID-normalization map from a vocabulary label 'hit in
the wild' -> a known-good OHDSI vocabulary_id.
  'ICD-10-CM'    -> ICD10CM
  WHO 'ICD-10'   -> ICD10
  'CPT' / 'CPT-4'-> CPT4

## It is a REGISTRY, not just a mapping — this is the load-bearing part
Every vocabulary label encountered is recorded VERBATIM, and each row resolves to EITHER a known-good
OHDSI vocabulary_id OR a **BLANK** id meaning 'not supported in OHDSI (as of now)'.

Ryan: 'if the vocab doesn't exist, we record it as it appears in the literature into that mapping file
and either derive a mapping or leave the mapping with no OHDSI ID to indicate that the vocab isn't
supported in OHDSI.'

Consequences that make the blank column worth the trouble:
- The table becomes the COMPLETE registry of labels seen + their OHDSI status. One source of truth.
- **A blank id IS litmine's non-OMOP gate** (lit-et6.3's extract-but-don't-produce set). No separate
  list needs maintaining.
- Provenance preserved (verbatim label is the key) and omission is VISIBLE — a blank loudly marks
  'not in OHDSI' instead of a code set silently vanishing (habitat rule 7).
- Blank means 'unsupported AS OF NOW' — revisitable when OHDSI or an OI supplemental vocab adds it.

## Seed data to build it from
- litmine's pilot produced **22 distinct vocabulary labels for ~14 real vocabularies** across 380
  code sets — that is the initial population, and it is real evidence rather than a guess.
- code_collector's vocab_mappings.csv (21 rows, name -> OHDSI id) eventually MIGRATES here.

## Constraints
- Keep this repo DATA-ONLY and polyglot. The consuming code lives in codesistant (cst-*), which reads
  both tables. Adding Python here would break the language-neutral value that is the whole point.
- 'Permissive' does NOT apply to this table — it is a plain lookup, not a regex.
- Keyed to the format regexes by OHDSI vocabulary_id.

## Downstream
Its non-blank ids can populate litmine's extraction-time vocabulary enum (lit-et6.4), which keeps the
enum and the format regexes from drifting apart. Build the enum FROM THIS DATA, not from a guess —
litmine's 'exposure' precedent (3rd-commonest role label, absent from the hand-written list) is the
cautionary case.

## Authoring
Hand the mappings to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary habitat.

## Before starting
Repo has stale uncommitted changes (see the sibling regex bead); reconcile them first.
close_reason: Delivered 2026-07-27 (commit 35cb6b1) as vocabulary_labels.tsv — 22 rows, keyed on the verbatim label, seeded from litmine's pilot. Carries the blank-vocabulary_id gate this bead specified, plus a status column separating 'unsupported' from 'multi_vocabulary' because they mean different things and have different remedies (wait for OHDSI vs split the code set). Named as a sibling of vocabulary_formats.tsv and picked up by the existing Makefile pattern rule, so no new convention. The bead's CPT4_HCPCS guidance is implemented: CPT, CPT-4, HCPCS and CPT/HCPCS all target the hybrid rather than the split ids, with the widening explained in the notes so nobody corrects it back. The 'mixed procedure codes... labeled only Procedures' label is flagged multi_vocabulary rather than mapped, as instructed — and a SECOND multi-vocabulary label was found that the bead did not anticipate ('ICD-9-CM / ICD-10-CM (mixed; printed as one unlabeled list)'). Most consequential finding: the two Korean labels are NOT unsupported — they map to OHDSI's EDI vocabulary (Korean HIRA, 442,551 concepts), verified by exact code matches, and left blank would have silently gated out 13 code sets. That corrects the worked example in litmine's lit-et6.3.

comments.author: Ryan Duryea
comments.text:
CPT4_HCPCS IS A FIRST-CLASS TARGET, AND PREFERRED FOR PROCEDURES (Ryan, 2026-07-25).

This bead says each row maps to 'a known-good OHDSI vocabulary_id'. Read literally that EXCLUDES the
hybrid procedure vocabulary and forces the naive mappings CPT->CPT4 and HCPCS->HCPCS, which re-creates
the exact split code_set_catalog's csc-171 exists to heal. Correct the wording: the target is a
vocabulary_id in OUR SUBSTRATE, which includes OI supplemental vocabularies.

VERIFIED against the June-2026 Athena build (vocabulation/synpuf_test_data.duckdb, schema ohdsi_vocabs):
    vocabulary_id      CPT4_HCPCS
    concepts           30,357
    CPT4 18,069 + HCPCS 12,822 = 30,891  ->  534 deduped
    vocabulary_version NULL  ->  OI supplemental, not stock Athena

Mark's framing in csc-171: 'I think of it as one system. And it's just because the AMA is a pain in
the ass that it's two systems. HCPCS without CPT is not helpful.'

ROWS THIS AFFECTS — real labels from litmine's 20-paper pilot:
    'CPT'        (23 code sets)  -> CPT4_HCPCS
    'CPT-4'       (6)            -> CPT4_HCPCS
    'HCPCS'       (4)            -> CPT4_HCPCS
    'CPT/HCPCS'   (1)            -> CPT4_HCPCS      <- has NO other home
    'mixed procedure codes (CPT, CPT Category III/PLA, HCPCS Level II, ICD-10-PCS); labeled only
     "Procedures" by the authors' (1) -> FLAG, do not guess. CPT4_HCPCS loses the ICD-10-PCS part,
     so this is probably a genuine multi-vocabulary set needing a producer-side split per habitat
     rule 4, not a single mapping.

Without the hybrid as a target, the last two resolve to BLANK and get silently dropped by
lit-et6.3's extract-but-don't-produce gate — losing a good procedure code set, the omission failure
habitat rule 7 calls the primary risk.

NOTE FOR THE notes COLUMN: mapping 'CPT' -> CPT4_HCPCS is a WIDENING (label says CPT, target covers
CPT+HCPCS). That is right for BINDING — a CPT code resolves in the hybrid — and loses nothing,
because the verbatim label remains the row key. State it explicitly so a later reader does not
'correct' it back to CPT4.

vocabulary_formats-3h8 (the matching format regex rows).

title: Extend format regexes to litmine's non-claims vocabularies (WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3)
description:
From seed vfm-6oo (decided by Ryan in litmine's lit-et6.1, 2026-07-23; filed here 2026-07-25).

## The gap
The table is 13 rows covering CLAIMS vocabularies only (ICD9CM, ICD10CM, HCPCS, CPT4, NDC + their
.DOTLESS / modifier / .ALPHANUM variants). litmine extracts code sets in whatever vocabulary a paper
used, so it needs rows for WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3, and whatever else
the corpus turns up. Ryan: 'tens of rows at most', cheap.

## HARD CONSTRAINT — keep them PERMISSIVE
Per this repo's README the regexes are deliberately skewed toward valid: accept anything that COULD
be a valid code, tolerate false positives, NEVER reject a real code. **False negatives are
unacceptable** (hence the loose ICD10CM \\w{3}.\\w{0,4} so future U-codes still pass).

Do NOT attempt strict/existence validation here. A regex validates FORMAT; it cannot validate
EXISTENCE — that is set-membership, answered only by the concept DB. You can't pattern your way to
'E11.9 is real but E11.99 is not', and a tight regex goes stale as codes change yearly.

The two layers together classify failures on different axes, which is more useful than either alone:
passes-format-but-misses-DB = well-formed but not real (typo / retired / non-US variant);
fails-format = malformed. That is litmine's validate.py taxonomy, already in production.

## Two field-tested constraints to inherit rather than rediscover
1. THE DOTTED-CODE TRAP — an undotted-only regex truncates 'M05.79' to category 'M05', collapsing a
   338-code list to ~12 hits. Every vocabulary needs BOTH forms covered. A consumer reading only one
   variant silently UNDER-COUNTS rather than erroring.
2. A >=4-CHARACTER FLOOR belongs in the CALLER, not here. It stops bare 3-char categories in disease
   prose ('F10', 'I21') matching during a scan — but a real 3-char code like 'I10' is legitimately
   valid, so putting the floor in the format regex would create exactly the false negative this repo
   forbids. Worth stating in the README as the regexes gain consumers; it is the kind of rule that
   gets pushed down into the shared layer by mistake.

## Mechanics
Edit vocabulary_formats.tsv; 'make all' regenerates the parquet. Keyed by OHDSI vocabulary_id, which
is also the join key to the id-normalization registry.

## Authoring
Hand the new regexes to a domain agent — Odie (OHDSI/OMOP) or Vincent (vocab) or the vocabulary
habitat — to author and validate. Do not guess them.

## Before starting
The repo has uncommitted changes (README.md, vocabulary_formats.tsv) plus untracked CLAUDE.md /
Makefile / vocabulary_formats.parquet, all with stale mtimes (2024 - 2026-02). Reconcile those first.
close_reason: Delivered 2026-07-27 (commit 35cb6b1). Format rows 13 -> 32: WHO ICD10, SNOMED, RxNorm + RxNorm Extension, ICD10PCS, ATC, DRG, ICD-O-3 morphology and topography, ICD9Proc, EDI, plus the OI hybrid CPT4_HCPCS and CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS as this bead's comment requested. Variants added where the data warranted (.DOTLESS, .WITHMODIFIERS, .UNPADDED, .NOBEHAVIOR). Authored by Odie, validated against real concept_codes in the June-2026 Athena build and re-checked through the shipped parquet; the 779 residual misses are enumerated per-row and are administrative artifacts rather than codes, deliberately not admitted. The CPT4_HCPCS proposals in the bead comment were confirmed as written (^\w{5}$ and ^(\w{5}|\w{2})$), and V-CPT / V-SRC were confirmed as UMLS source markers to exclude — with 7 more of the same family found. Two pre-existing false negatives fixed in passing, both outside this bead's scope: NDC rejected 338,328 real codes (26% of the vocabulary) and CPT4 rejected M0201. Ryan's review then split NDC and SNOMED into claims-default plus full-vocabulary variants per the vfm-k2n principle.

comments.author: Ryan Duryea
comments.text:
ADD CPT4_HCPCS ROWS TOO (Ryan, 2026-07-25) — the hybrid procedure vocabulary has no format regex.

This bead scopes the non-claims vocabularies. Add the hybrid alongside them: OI's CPT4_HCPCS
(code_set_catalog csc-171 — CPT4 and HCPCS unioned and deduped because the digit/letter partition is
administrative, not clinical). It exists in the substrate with 30,357 concepts, but vocabulary_formats
still splits them, so a producer canonicalizing a hybrid code has nothing to validate against.

MEASURED against the 25,850 five-character CPT4_HCPCS concept_codes:
    existing CPT4   ^\d{4}\w$   matches 13,670 / 25,850
    existing HCPCS  ^\w\d{4}$   matches 23,436 / 25,850
    candidate       ^\w{5}$      matches 25,848 / 25,850
Neither existing row covers the hybrid; the union pattern does.

The 2 stragglers are 'V-CPT' and 'V-SRC' — OMOP administrative concepts, NOT procedure codes. Do not
widen the regex to admit them; confirm they should be excluded rather than matched.

Non-5-char entries in the vocabulary are modifiers ('0A', '0B', ...), so mirror the existing pattern
with a .WITHMODIFIERS variant:
    CPT4_HCPCS                 ^\w{5}$
    CPT4_HCPCS.WITHMODIFIERS   ^(\w{5}|\w{2})$
Both proposed, not decided — validate against the real concept_codes before committing, per the
procedure now documented in this repo's CLAUDE.md. Note ^\w{5}$ is DELIBERATELY permissive: it
admits both digit-leading (CPT) and letter-leading (HCPCS) codes, which is the entire point of the
hybrid, and matches this repo's never-reject-a-real-code rule.

Keyed by vocabulary_id, so these rows also become the join target for the id-normalization registry
(vocabulary_formats-e5s), where CPT4_HCPCS is the PREFERRED mapping for procedure labels.

Related: csc-171, csc-meqj, vocabulary_formats-e5s.
